title: Acute limb ischaemia: vascular examination
stem: Cubicle 28. Mr Fung, 72, with atrial fibrillation (stopped his anticoagulant a month ago), has had sudden severe pain in his right leg for 3 hours; the leg is cold and he says it feels numb. Examine his lower limbs and explain your plan.

phases.title: Examine
phases.goal: Both legs: the 6 Ps, pulses and Doppler.

phases.title: Plan
phases.goal: Threatened limb: what now, and what next?

review.text: Chronic versus acute. Your vascular notes (Buerger's test, ABPI, DVT management) fit chronic ischaemia and DVT. For an acutely threatened limb, the priorities are the 6 Ps and Rutherford grade, immediate IV heparin, and urgent vascular surgery; ABPI and Buerger's test do not belong in that station.

notes:
Checked against the ESVS 2020 guideline on acute limb ischaemia, NICE CG147 (peripheral arterial disease) and the Rutherford classification.

The 6 Ps: pain, pallor, pulselessness, perishingly cold, paraesthesia, paralysis. Sensory loss and weakness (Rutherford IIa/IIb) mean the limb is threatened; fixed mottling, paralysis and anaesthesia mean it is irreversible (III). Embolic ischaemia (AF, sudden, no claudication history, normal contralateral pulses) versus thrombotic (claudication history, reduced contralateral pulses). Examine: inspection (colour, mottling, blanching), temperature (level), capillary refill, all pulses (femoral, popliteal, DP, PT) both sides, handheld Doppler (arterial and venous signals), sensation and motor function, calf tenderness (compartment). Treatment: immediate IV unfractionated heparin (e.g. 5000 units bolus) unless contraindicated, analgesia, urgent vascular surgery (embolectomy, thrombolysis, or bypass within hours for threatened limbs), watch for reperfusion (hyperkalaemia, compartment syndrome).

Your vascular notes cover inspection, pulses, Buerger's test, ABPI and DVT management — which apply to chronic ischaemia and DVT; for the acute threatened limb, the priority is heparin and immediate vascular referral.

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Compare both legs: colour, temperature, CRT, pulses, Doppler, sensation, power, calf.

Look and feel.r: Right foot and calf pale and mottled (blanches with pressure).
Right leg cold below the mid-thigh.
Look and feel.mark: Compares temperature and finds the level

Pulses.t: Femoral, popliteal, dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial — both sides
Pulses.r: Right femoral present; right popliteal and foot pulses absent. Left all present.
Pulses.mark: Palpates all pulses on both sides

Pulses.r: No arterial signal at the right ankle; venous signal present.
Pulses.mark: Uses Doppler for arterial and venous signals

Neuro.r: Reduced light touch over the right foot; weak toe dorsiflexion.
Neuro.mark: Assesses sensory and motor deficit (threatened limb)
Neuro.do: cotton foot-R,toes-R & say toes | pin foot-R,toes-R & say toes

Heart.mark: Identifies AF as an embolic source

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings and your plan.
steps.label: Plan
steps.hint: Acute embolic ischaemia, threatened limb (Rutherford IIb): heparin, analgesia, vascular surgery now.

opts.t: Acute embolic limb ischaemia from AF, threatened (sensory and motor loss)
opts.mark: Diagnoses acute embolic ischaemia and grades it

opts.t: IV unfractionated heparin bolus now; IV analgesia; bloods including group and save, CK, lactate
Emergency vascular surgery referral for revascularisation within hours
Arterial duplex next week in clinic
opts.r: A threatened limb has hours, not days.

qs.a: Pain, pallor, pulselessness, perishingly cold, paraesthesia, paralysis
wrong: Pain, pus, purpura, pyrexia, pallor, paralysis
Pulse, pressure, perfusion, pain, plasma, platelets
Pallor, puffiness, petechiae, pain, pyrexia, paralysis

qs.q: Sign of an irreversibly ischaemic limb?
wrong: Absent foot pulses alone, with normal sensation

qs.q: Clue to embolic rather than thrombotic ischaemia?
qs.a: Sudden onset, AF, normal contralateral pulses

wrong: Calcified, incompressible vessels at the ankle

qs.q: First drug in acute limb ischaemia?
wrong: Thrombolysis in the ED for all
